**Make the relentless pursuit of accurate understanding of reality the highest cultural priority—above comfort, status, ideology, or tribal loyalty.**

Almost every large-scale human problem is made worse (or created) by motivated reasoning, suppressed information, false models of the world, and incentives that reward looking right over being right. Poverty, conflict, preventable disease, bad policy, technological stagnation, and even many environmental issues improve dramatically when people and institutions update on evidence instead of defending narratives. Truth-seeking is upstream of better decisions in science, governance, economics, and personal life.

### Why this over more common wishes
- Ending war, poverty, or disease sounds noble, but those are downstream. You can't reliably solve them while operating on systematically wrong maps of reality (incentives, human nature, physics, biology, trade-offs). History is full of well-intentioned catastrophes built on bad models.
- Abundant clean energy, better biotech, multiplanetary capability, or advanced AI would be transformative. They become far more likely and safer when societies reward curiosity, falsifiability, and open criticism rather than dogma or prestige.
- Free speech and intellectual humility aren't side issues; they are prerequisites. Without the ability to challenge sacred claims and admit error, "progress" becomes theater or coercion.

This isn't a call for cold rationalism that ignores human values or emotions. Values still matter enormously—what we *do* with better maps is a separate question of ethics and preference. It is a claim that accurate maps beat inaccurate ones for almost any coherent goal, and that cultures which treat truth as non-negotiable (even when it hurts) compound advantages over time. xAI's own mission—understanding the true nature of the universe—rests on exactly this: curiosity and evidence over comforting stories.

Trade-offs exist. Truth can be temporarily demoralizing or destabilizing. Status games and coalitions often outcompete pure inquiry in the short run. Implementing a culture shift is hard because it requires changing incentives, education, media, and prestige hierarchies. But if I get one lever, it's the one that multiplies the effectiveness of every other lever.

What would *you* change, and why that over the alternatives?
